chapter: Small's Paradise, Fletcher Henderson and Horace
title: Fletcher Henderson's difficult arrangements and Charlie Dixon's hard keys
summary: Arrangements by Don Redman and Charlie Dixon were in hard keys; Fletcher wrote easier ones, and the early ones were rough.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah, that's -- well, by this time, of course, I mean you'd had a lot of experience, so, you know, you were going into these bands --
-- reading arrangements. Did you find Fletcher's -- a lot of people have said Fletcher's arrangements were hard.

Well, you know, Don would put them in those like what we say concert keys like E natural or B natural, working four, five sharps. So you get, [like you do the thing] -- like when a fellow come in town, just say, well, just start with C, play in the key of C and keep on going. See how long they'd last. (Unintelligible).
(Unintelligible) music. But what about -- I mean originally most of those arrangements of Fletcher's were by (unintelligible) Don Redman --
And Charlie was -- oh, he loved to
He -- that's right. He just loved to stick you.
Yeah. Well now, but what about Fletcher himself when he starts to write?
Fletcher would write very nice. He (unintelligible) like the key of G or something like that or maybe three or four sharps, but not like Charlie Dixon. Charlie write them five sharps.

He even write them for the show. I used to call him -- I says, hey, Charlie, I said, what are you going to do cut us (unintelligible) rehearsing the show up where tonight? We'd be pretty restless, you know. Looked at me and say, Hap, you playing down there with Fletcher, that's what. Yeah, they are. he write that way. He could (unintelligible) --
I mean did Fletcher write in hard keys too?
He could if he wanted to.
They all seem to flow very easily. I mean Don's things --
Especially -- I mean those early days --
-- like in '28 they were rough arrangements.
And they were too -- I mean they didn't swing because they couldn't swing them.
No, they didn't. But he was my favorite, Don was. He was such a fine guy.
